chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughirah, from Humran ibn A'yan, who said:
Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام) said: Indeed, 'Ali (عليه السلام) was a Muhaddath.

So I went out to my companions and said, 'I have come to you with something astonishing.' They said, 'And what is it?' I said, 'I heard Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام) saying: 'Ali (عليه السلام) was a Muhaddath.' They said, 'You have done nothing unless you ask him who it was that used to speak to him.' So I returned to him and said, 'I conveyed to my companions what you had conveyed to me, and they said: You have done nothing unless you ask him who it was that used to speak to him.'

So he said to me, 'An angel used to speak to him.' I said, 'Are you saying that he was a Prophet?' He said, then he moved his hand like this: 'Or like the companion of Sulayman, or like the companion of Musa, or like Dhu al-Qarnayn.'
Or has it not reached you that he said: 'And among you is one like him.'

key_terms.ذِي الْقَرْنَيْنِ: Dhu al-Qarnayn, cited as another example of a specially guided figure
key_terms.صَاحِبِ سُلَيْمَانَ: the companion of Sulayman cited as a comparable example
key_terms.صَاحِبِ مُوسَى: the companion of Musa cited as a comparable example
key_terms.مَلَكٌ: an angel who communicated with him
key_terms.مُحَدَّثًا: one spoken to by an angel or recipient of divine communication
key_terms.نَبِيٌّ: a Prophet; mentioned here to distinguish divine communication from prophethood

ai.seo_question: What does it mean that Imam 'Ali (عليه السلام) was مُحَدَّثًا, and does that imply prophethood?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Imam 'Ali (عليه السلام) was مُحَدَّثًا, meaning that an angel spoke to him, while clarifying that this does not necessarily mean prophethood. The report places him alongside figures who received divine communication without being presented here as Prophets, highlighting his extraordinary spiritual rank and knowledge.
